elements.scope_reason: Red-box header 'Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA' -> Urgent priority for new stroke/TIA.
elements.problem: Urgent is encoded for sudden-onset stroke symptoms and for TIA qualified 'New', but also for an UNQUALIFIED (clinical_finding Cerebrovascular accident). Descendants and qualified forms match, so a patient attending for routine care of a PREVIOUS stroke (the subject of the rest of this page) would be triaged Urgent. The page limits urgency to a NEW stroke/TIA; the CVA evidence should carry the 'New' qualifier (as TIA does) or a recent-onset time criterion. Urgent level itself is justified.
evidence: Urgent: new stroke/TIA :: (or ... (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Cerebrovascular accident" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Transient ischemic attack" "disorder") (qualifier (snomed_concept "New" "qualifier value"))))

elements.scope_reason: management_step: SpO2 < 94% / RR >= 30 are thresholds for giving oxygen to an already-urgent patient, not a triage or diagnostic criterion; SpO2 and RR are routine vitals.
cross_reference_only: glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetic) routes to hypoglycaemia page 19, where that logic lives; glucose is a routine vital.
management_step: avoid treating BP >= 140/90; BP >= 220/120 -> discuss pre-referral treatment. No priority escalation stated by the page.
management_step: within 3 hours -> refer urgently for thrombolysis (referral routing, not triage).
management_step: refer same day, aspirin 300 mg with its contraindications.
'Sudden onset of one or more of the following suggests a stroke (or TIA if < 24 h and resolved)' is diagnostic logic.
parts_missing: TIA branch: no diagnosis rule for Transient ischemic attack (symptoms lasted < 24 hours and resolved completely); TIA appears only as a 'New' check_for item consumed by the priority rule

elements.problem: Stroke part correct: all four bullets split into 15 sudden-onset findings (face/arm/leg weakness and numbness; blurred, decreased vision, diplopia; difficulty speaking, understanding; difficulty walking, dizziness, balance, co-ordination) combined with 'or' into a possible CVA rule; all concepts exist. 'Suggests' encoded as possible is defensible (borderline vs probable). The TIA conclusion is missing.

rule_level_problems.problem: Unqualified (clinical_finding Cerebrovascular accident) as priority evidence makes any recorded stroke (incl. a known/previous stroke attending routine care, or any of its 51+ descendants) Urgent. Inconsistent with the TIA evidence, which carries 'New'. Should be CVA + 'New' qualifier (and checked for) or a recent-onset time criterion.

No diagnosis rule for Transient ischemic attack although the page defines it (stroke symptoms lasting < 24 hours and resolved completely); the onset/time-based form or a possible TIA rule from the same sudden-onset findings is missing.

Task is triggered by unqualified common symptom Dizziness (and other unqualified findings), so every dizzy patient gets the stroke check list; acceptable pre-screen pattern but noisy. Its due_to also includes unqualified CVA, so a known previous stroke will re-open the new-stroke check list each visit.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible stroke from sudden-onset neurological symptoms
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Suggests a stroke' encoded as possible; because it is possible, the priority rule cannot reference it via active_condition and duplicates all 15 findings instead. Defensible, but probable would be equally readable from 'suggests'. Unilaterality ('especially on one side') not captured.

summary: The priority rule (and check-task trigger) accept an unqualified 'Cerebrovascular accident', so a patient with a previous stroke attending routine care would be triaged Urgent, contrary to the page's 'new stroke/TIA' scope (TIA is correctly qualified 'New', CVA is not). The TIA definition (< 24 h, resolved completely) has no diagnosis rule. The stroke symptom list itself is fully and correctly encoded with valid SNOMED concepts; all other red-box bullets are management steps out of scope.
